title: Component Ops Contract v1
description: What a component tells Ops about how it is operated. Owned and versioned by the component's own repository; Ops only consumes it, and checks the things no single component can check about itself.

component_id.description: The source id Ops already knows this component by. Checked against the directory the file was found in, so a copied contract cannot make one component answer for another.

units.description: The systemd units this component owns. The unit files themselves still live in eidolon_kernel/deploy/systemd; this is the declaration Ops checks them against, so a unit pointing at the wrong venv or a stale port stops being something only a Host discovers.

id.description: The systemd unit name without its .service suffix.

kind.description: platform: a unit the host profile installs rather than a release — an upstream server with no repository of ours. It is the one kind allowed an absolute exec, because where it lives IS a platform fact.

exec.description: The executable, relative to this component's deployed root. Absolute paths are refused for anything a release ships: where a component is unpacked is a platform-profile fact, not the component's.

user.description: The account the unit runs as. Stated per unit because one component can own units with different accounts — Admin runs its bootstrap daemon as a separate user precisely so a compromise there cannot read the rest.

requires.description: Units that must be pulled in and ordered before this one (systemd Wants= plus After=).

after.description: Units this one is ordered behind without depending on (systemd After= alone).

serves.description: Port roles this unit listens on, drawn from this component's own [ports].

ports.description: Roles, not numbers. A component says it needs somewhere to listen and what that place is for; the number is a default the Host may override, because two Hosts may disagree and neither disagreement is the component's business.

inputs.description: The files Ops installs for this component before it can start: generated env files, settings overlays, key material. Names only — a contract is committed to a repository, so anything written here is public to everyone who can read it.

name.description: The id Ops stages this input under.

install_path.description: The one absolute path it is written to. Absolute rather than relative to a config root because two of these are not under one: key material lives with the state it authenticates.

kind.description: secret: generated credentials. settings: a component settings file the Host overlay rewrites. identity: long-lived key material that survives reinstall.

source.description: operator: staged from the operator's private inputs directory, and an install cannot proceed without it. derived: Ops renders it on the way to the Host from a template in this repository, so there is nothing for an operator to supply.

template.description: For derived inputs: the template's repository-relative path, so Ops does not have to know this component's layout. It is a path in THIS repository and there is no way to name another one: a component whose deployed defaults live in someone else's repository cannot change them without that repository's release, and the copy its own tests exercise is then not the copy a Host starts with. Hub was in exactly that position, and the two files had drifted before anyone read them side by side.

required_by.description: Unit ids that will not start without it.

authority.description: What this component would be sorry to lose. Every entry has to say how it is backed up, and an entry that cannot be backed up has to say why — see the backup enum.

path.description: Absolute, because this is a Host location an operator will read in a report and type into a shell.

backup.description: sqlite-online: snapshot consistently while the owning service keeps running. quiesce-copy: stop the units in quiesce_units, copy, start again. none: not carried, and uncovered_reason must say what would be needed.

uncovered_reason.description: Required when backup is none. A backup that silently omits something restores into a system that looks whole and is not, which is worse than one that says what it left out.

runtime.description: Absolute paths that are safe to delete at any moment. Named so a reset does not have to guess which side of the line a directory falls on.

schema.description: How this component brings its own persistent schema up to date, if it has one. There is deliberately no way to declare a downgrade: incompatible legacy data is rebuilt rather than migrated backwards.

reset.description: What a factory reset removes for this component. Ops refuses to run one at all while any component is silent, because a reset believed to be complete is worse than one known to be impossible.

artifacts.description: What this component needs on a Host that is not in its git tree — model weights, prebuilt binaries. Declared because a release is exact git commits, so whatever is not in git does not exist in a release, and that gap should be stated by the component rather than found by an operator on a board with no network.
